title: Stalks of the inverse image of a sheaf along a continuous map, with germs
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map of topological spaces and let $\mathcal C$ be the category of abelian groups or the category of commutative rings. For a sheaf $\mathcal G$ on $Y$ with values in $\mathcal C$ let $f^{-1}\mathcal G$ be its inverse image, the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of the presheaf $f_p\mathcal G:U\mapsto\varinjlim_{V\supseteq f(U)}\mathcal G(V)$, and let $\eta_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G\to f_*f^{-1}\mathcal G$ be the unit of the adjunction $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ (so $\eta_{\mathcal G,V}:\mathcal G(V)\to(f^{-1}\mathcal G)(f^{-1}V)$ for $V\subseteq Y$ open), all as in [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image]. Stalks and germs are those of [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] (for commutative rings, the colimit over the open neighbourhoods taken in commutative rings). Then for every $x\in X$, with $y=f(x)$, there is an isomorphism in $\mathcal C$
$$c_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G_y\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }(f^{-1}\mathcal G)_x,$$
natural in $\mathcal G$, such that $c_{\mathcal G}(s_y)=(\eta_{\mathcal G,V}(s))_x$ for every open $V\ni y$ and every $s\in\mathcal G(V)$. In particular every element of $(f^{-1}\mathcal G)_x$ is the germ at $x$ of $\eta_{\mathcal G,V}(s)$ for some open $V\ni y$ and some $s\in\mathcal G(V)$.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma Tag 008H (label lemma-stalk-pullback: $(f^{-1}\mathcal G)_x=\mathcal G_{f(x)}$), proved from Lemma Tag 008G (lemma-stalk-pullback-presheaf, the colimit computation $(f_p\mathcal G)_x=\varinjlim_{x\in U}\varinjlim_{f(U)\subseteq V}\mathcal G(V)=\mathcal G_{f(x)}$) and stalks commute with sheafification (lemma-stalk-sheafification); the germ formula is the construction (the map $\mathcal G(V)\to f_p\mathcal G(f^{-1}V)$ is the presheaf unit)

proof.text: *(0) Set-up.* Write $y=f(x)$. By [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image], $f^{-1}\mathcal G=(f_p\mathcal G)^\#$ with sheafification map $\theta=\theta_{\mathcal G}:f_p\mathcal G\to f^{-1}\mathcal G$ (a morphism of presheaves on $X$ with values in $\mathcal C$), $i_{\mathcal G,V}:\mathcal G(V)\to f_p\mathcal G(f^{-1}V)$ is the coprojection of index $V$, and the unit is $\eta_{\mathcal G,V}=\theta_{f^{-1}V}\circ i_{\mathcal G,V}$ for every open $V\subseteq Y$.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 008F (the map $i_{\mathcal G}$ in its proof) and the definition $f^{-1}\mathcal G=(f_p\mathcal G)^\#$ with the adjunction after Lemma 008G; Sections 008N, 008P

proof.text: *(1) Stalks of the presheaf inverse image.* By [lem-weil-pbc-presheaf-inverse-image-stalk] applied to $\mathcal G$ (a sheaf, in particular a presheaf with values in $\mathcal C$) there is an isomorphism $c^p:\mathcal G_y\to(f_p\mathcal G)_x$ in $\mathcal C$ with $c^p(s_y)=(i_{\mathcal G,V}(s))_x$ for every open $V\ni y$ and $s\in\mathcal G(V)$.

*(2) Stalks commute with sheafification.* The stalk map $\theta_x:(f_p\mathcal G)_x\to(f^{-1}\mathcal G)_x$, $t_x\mapsto(\theta_U(t))_x$ for $t\in f_p\mathcal G(U)$, $x\in U$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], is an isomorphism in $\mathcal C$: for abelian groups by [lem-weil-pbc-stalk-sheafification-space] applied on $X$ to the presheaf $f_p\mathcal G$; for commutative rings by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-stalk-sheafification-space] applied to the presheaf of commutative rings $f_p\mathcal G$.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 007Z (lemma-stalk-sheafification), as used in the proof of Lemma 008H

proof.text: *(3) The isomorphism and the germ formula.* Put $c_{\mathcal G}=\theta_x\circ c^p:\mathcal G_y\to(f^{-1}\mathcal G)_x$, an isomorphism in $\mathcal C$ as a composite of the isomorphisms of steps (1) and (2). For an open $V\ni y$ and $s\in\mathcal G(V)$, steps (1), (2) and (0) give $c_{\mathcal G}(s_y)=\theta_x((i_{\mathcal G,V}(s))_x)=(\theta_{f^{-1}V}(i_{\mathcal G,V}(s)))_x=(\eta_{\mathcal G,V}(s))_x$.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 008H (lemma-stalk-pullback: 'a combination of Lemmas 007Z and 008G'); the germ formula is written out by the worker

proof.text: *(4) Every element is such a germ.* Every element of $\mathcal G_y$ is a germ $s_y$ with $s\in\mathcal G(V)$ for some open $V\ni y$: for abelian groups by [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]; for commutative rings by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise] (2) with $R=\mathbb Z$ (commutative rings are the commutative $\mathbb Z$-algebras), the open neighbourhoods of $y$ forming a directed set. Since $c_{\mathcal G}$ is surjective, every element of $(f^{-1}\mathcal G)_x$ is $c_{\mathcal G}(s_y)=(\eta_{\mathcal G,V}(s))_x$ by step (3).

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 008H; written out by the worker

proof.text: *(5) Naturality.* Let $u:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$ be a morphism of sheaves on $Y$ with values in $\mathcal C$. The unit is natural: $(f^{-1}u)_{f^{-1}V}\circ\eta_{\mathcal G,V}=\eta_{\mathcal G',V}\circ u_V$, since by [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] $(f^{-1}u)\circ\theta_{\mathcal G}=\theta_{\mathcal G'}\circ f_pu$ and $(f_pu)_{f^{-1}V}\circ i_{\mathcal G,V}=i_{\mathcal G',V}\circ u_V$ (the defining property of $f_pu$ on coprojections), and step (0). The stalk maps of [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] satisfy $u_y(s_y)=(u_V(s))_y$ and $(f^{-1}u)_x(t_x)=((f^{-1}u)_U(t))_x$. Hence for $s\in\mathcal G(V)$, $V\ni y$, by step (3): $c_{\mathcal G'}(u_y(s_y))=(\eta_{\mathcal G',V}(u_V(s)))_x=((f^{-1}u)_{f^{-1}V}(\eta_{\mathcal G,V}(s)))_x=(f^{-1}u)_x(c_{\mathcal G}(s_y))$. The two morphisms $c_{\mathcal G'}\circ u_y$ and $(f^{-1}u)_x\circ c_{\mathcal G}$ agree on all germs, which exhaust $\mathcal G_y$ (step (4)), so they are equal: $c$ is natural in $\mathcal G$.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 008H ('canonical bijection'; naturality not spelled out in the source); written out by the worker
